name: Cloudflare Sandbox SDK / Containers

modes.label: Pay-as-you-go (active CPU, provisioned RAM/disk)
modes.note: CPU $0.00002/vCPU-s on active usage only (since 2025-11-21); memory $0.0000025/GiB-s and disk $0.00000007/GB-s ($0.000252/GB-h) on provisioned size while running, 10 ms granularity. Custom types: 1-4 vCPU, >=3 GiB/vCPU, <=12 GiB, <=20 GB disk; presets lite(1/16 vCPU,256MiB) basic(1/4,1GiB) standard-1(1/2,4GiB) standard-2(1,6GiB) standard-3(2,8GiB) standard-4(4,12GiB,20GB). 4 vCPU/8 GiB forces 12 GiB. Provisioned disk (~$0.005/h for 20 GB) is NOT in these rates. boot_overhead_s = ~2 s cold start (docs: billing starts at request; 1-3 s; ComputeSDK median 2.0 s). Default sleepAfter = 10 min idle tail billed at RAM+disk (not modelled). keepAlive always-on uses the same rates (no commit discount). Basis verified 2026-09-28: CPU billed on "active usage only"; memory and disk on "provisioned resources for the instance type you select"; "Charges stop after the container instance goes to sleep, which can happen automatically after a timeout." (https://developers.cloudflare.com/containers/pricing/). Sleep after "a period of inactivity (10 minutes by default, configurable via sleepAfter)" (https://developers.cloudflare.com/sandbox/concepts/sandboxes/).

evidence.quote: By default, a Container will allow internet access, and you can set `deniedHosts` to disallow specific hosts or IPs.

plans.name: Workers Free
plans.note: Containers / Sandbox not available on Free (N/A).

plans.name: Workers Paid
plans.note: $5/mo account minimum, not a credit. Includes 375 vCPU-min ($0.45) + 25 GiB-h ($0.225) + 200 GB-h disk ($0.0504) of Containers per month (resource-specific, expressed here as $0.7254), plus 10M Worker requests, 30M Worker CPU-ms, 1M DO requests, 400k DO GB-s, 20M log events. Concurrency is resource-capped per account: 1,500 vCPU / 6 TiB RAM / 30 TB disk running (=375 standard-4), raisable.

plans.name: Enterprise
plans.note: Workers Enterprise billed per contract; rates not published.

perf_source: ComputeSDK (github.com/computesdk/benchmarks results/): cold 2,000.55 ms (seq TTI 2026-08-07), burst 647.84 ms (2026-09-25); instance type set by the benchmark's own deployed Worker (not in repo). DAX never succeeded; no HPC result.

knobs.label: sleepAfter idle tail (x session hours)
knobs.why: A container stays awake until sleepAfter expires after the last request (default 10 min). During that tail provisioned RAM and disk bill at full size (CPU is active-only, so ~$0). Factor = (session + tail) / session: default 10 min on 30-min sessions = 1.33x, on 10-min bursts = 2x. Slightly overstates because the engine also applies util-scaled CPU to the tail. The card does not model the tail by default (1).

caveats: 4 vCPU / 8 GiB is not offered: >=3 GiB RAM per vCPU, so 4 vCPU always pays 12 GiB; max shape 4 vCPU/12 GiB/20 GB.
Default sleepAfter is 10 min: RAM+disk bill at full size during the idle tail after each activity burst (~$0.113/h for standard-4); keepAlive bills continuously with no cap.

Sleep wipes all state (no paused state). Persistence = directory backups to your own R2 bucket, billed at R2 Standard $0.015/GB-month after 10 GB-month free (+ Class A $4.50/M, Class B $0.36/M after free tiers); backup TTL does not delete R2 objects. Whole-container snapshots are private beta, unpriced.

Each sandbox is a Durable Object: $0.15/M requests after 1M, $12.50/M GB-s after 400k GB-s at 128 MB; if awake for the whole container run ~ $0.00576/h per sandbox (unverified). Worker requests $0.30/M after 10M; Workers Logs $0.60/M after 20M. Third-party estimate: +5-10%.
Egress free allotment/rate vary by region: NA/EU 1 TB then $0.025/GB; Oceania/Korea/Taiwan 500 GB then $0.05/GB; elsewhere 500 GB then $0.04/GB. Card uses NA/EU.
Instance type is per container class at deploy time, not per sandbox.
No guaranteed runtime: irregular host restarts stop instances (SIGTERM, 15 min grace) and wipe state.
Concurrency limited by account resource caps (1,500 vCPU / 6 TiB / 30 TB), not a sandbox count.
perf.cpu_runs_s: no hpc benchmark for Cloudflare; dax never succeeded in ComputeSDK runs.
open_source refers to the SDK/container server/bridge only; platform is proprietary and cannot be self-hosted.

Verifier 2026-09-28: storage.included_disk_gib was 20 (engine treated 20 GB as free). Cloudflare bills provisioned disk at $0.00000007/GB-s while the container runs (https://developers.cloudflare.com/containers/pricing/), so included_disk_gib -> 0 and disk_gib_month -> 0.18396 (= $0.000252/GB-h x 730); with disk_billed_when_stopped=false the engine bills it only for running hours, which matches. The 200 GB-h/month included disk sits inside Workers Paid included_usd. Max disk is 20 GB (<= 2 GB per GiB RAM), which the engine does not enforce.
Verifier 2026-09-28: snapshot_free_gib_account = 10 added (R2 Standard 10 GB-month free, https://developers.cloudflare.com/r2/pricing/).
Account concurrency caps (1,500 vCPU / 6 TiB / 30 TB) and per-sandbox Durable Object / Worker request charges are not modelled by the engine.

Per container class, wrangler max_instances defaults to 20 concurrently running instances; a start request beyond it errors. Self-serve config change up to the account caps (1,500 vCPU / 6 TiB / 30 TB).

Durable Object usage above the included amount is rounded up to the next billable unit (1M GB-s / 1M requests) before the rate applies, so the first DO overage is at least $12.50 (duration) or $0.15 (requests).
root=true means uid 0 inside an unprivileged container: no privileged mode, Docker only via docker:dind-rootless with iptables disabled, no kernel modules.

Worker subrequests are not billed; each Sandbox SDK operation is an RPC call on the sandbox's Durable Object stub and is billed as one DO request ($0.15/M after the 1M/month included), not as a Worker request.

DO duration may not run for the whole container lifetime: DOs idle and eligible for hibernation are not billed for duration, and an inactivity timeout can keep the container running while the DO sleeps. The ~$0.00576/h per-sandbox DO estimate is an upper bound.

fleet.tiers: Free unavailable; Workers Paid: 1,500 aggregate vCPU, 6 TiB RAM, 30 TB disk per account. Higher limits via account team, support ticket or form.
fleet.notes: default_max_vcpu=0 is free-account access, not paid capacity. Paid pool is 1,500 vCPU (not an instance count); at 4 vCPU each, CPU alone permits 375 instances, with memory/disk constraints also applied. No promise of an auto-approved quota form or turnaround.

audit_2026_09_29.source: checked against the provider's live pricing and docs pages

snapshot_auto.quote: After a period of inactivity (10 minutes by default, configurable via sleepAfter), the container stops to free resources. When the next request arrives, a fresh container starts. All previous state is lost and the environment resets to its initial state.
snapshot_auto.note: Platform wipes state on sleep. Auto-save-on-idle exists only as app code you write: lifecycle hook onActivityExpired() calling createBackup() (Cloudflare's claude-managed-agents template does this), or the OpenAI Agents API template calling the private-beta container.snapshotContainer() on an idle webhook ('a confirmed idle session creates a whole-container snapshot before its container stops'). Not a platform default.

snapshot_on_demand.quote: Create point-in-time snapshots of sandbox directories and restore them from R2.
snapshot_on_demand.note: GA (2026-02-23): createBackup({dir}) -> squashfs in your own R2 bucket; restoreBackup() mounts it as copy-on-write FUSE overlay (lost on sleep, re-restore each wake). Directory-level only (under /workspace, /home, /tmp, /var/tmp, /app), no memory/processes. Can seed other sandboxes: changelog says 'Usable across multiple instances - Fork a backup across many sandboxes for parallel work'. Whole-container snapshots (container.snapshotContainer(), restore via start({containerSnapshot})) are private beta: 'Container snapshots are currently in private beta' (openai-agents-api tutorial); no memory documented.

harness_api.quote: Starts an OpenCode server inside a Sandbox container.
harness_api.note: OpenCode only: first-party SDK export @cloudflare/sandbox/opencode (createOpencodeServer, createOpencode -> typed @opencode-ai/sdk client with session.create/session.prompt/events, proxyToOpencode for the web UI). Listed on docs as a first-party extension on the 1.0 preview ('OpenCode | @cloudflare/sandbox/opencode'). Claude Code tutorial just runs `claude --print` via exec (not a harness API). Codex via OpenAI Agents API and Claude Managed Agents: Cloudflare is only the self-hosted execution environment; the harness API belongs to OpenAI/Anthropic.

egress_allowlist.quote: When allowedHosts is set, it becomes a deny-by-default allowlist. Any host or IP not in the list is denied, and only matching destinations can reach outbound or outboundByHost handlers.
egress_allowlist.note: Per Sandbox class plus per-instance at runtime (setAllowedHosts/allowHost/denyHost). Hostnames with globs and IPs/CIDRs (example deniedHosts includes "141.101.64.0/18"). enableInternet=false: 'Only ports 80, 443, and DNS are available, and DNS queries use Cloudflare's DNS servers.' Enforced by a sidecar/Workers runtime outside the sandbox.

egress_http_rules.quote: Add custom policy on outbound traffic (such as denying specific HTTP requests)
egress_http_rules.note: outbound / outboundByHost handlers are arbitrary Workers code seeing the full Request (docs example blocks non-GET methods). HTTPS interception on by default (interceptHttps=true, per-instance ephemeral CA). HTTP/HTTPS only; other ports never routed through handlers.

ingress_rules.quote: Preview URLs are publicly accessible by default, but require a valid access token that is generated when you expose a port.
ingress_rules.note: Only ports you exposePort() get a URL (https://{port}-{sandbox-id}-{token}.yourdomain.com); every request goes through your own Worker (proxyToSandbox) so you can add auth; unexposePort() revokes. Quick tunnels (*.trycloudflare.com) have no auth beyond the random hostname. No IP allowlist setting; no raw TCP/UDP inbound.

guest_firewall.quote: Cloudflare Containers do not support iptables manipulation.
guest_firewall.note: Root inside an unprivileged container (in a per-container VM); same statement on https://developers.cloudflare.com/containers/faq/. Docker-in-Docker requires dockerd --iptables=false.

secret_proxy.quote: Because outbound handlers run in the Workers runtime — outside the sandbox — they can hold secrets that the sandbox itself never sees. The sandbox makes a plain HTTP request, and the handler attaches the credential before forwarding it to the upstream service.
secret_proxy.note: Any host, per-instance keys via ctx.containerId; HTTPS covered via TLS interception. Not covered: non-HTTP ('Outbound handlers only intercept HTTP and HTTPS traffic'), so no DB/SSH credential injection (git over HTTPS works). Also mountBucket credentialProxy:true re-signs S3/GCS requests so bucket keys never enter the container. It is a mechanism you program (Workers code), not a managed secret registry. OpenCode example injects the Anthropic key this way.

volume_attach.quote: Mount S3-compatible object storage buckets as local filesystem paths.
volume_attach.note: Only S3-compatible bucket mounts via FUSE (s3fs): R2 by Worker binding (no credentials in container), or S3/GCS/B2/MinIO endpoints; prefix + readOnly options. No block or network volumes; disk fixed by instance type (max 20 GB).

volume_shared.quote: Multiple sandboxes access the same data
volume_shared.note: Same bucket mountable in many sandboxes at once; read-write or read-only ('Protect data by mounting buckets in read-only mode'). Object-store semantics (s3fs), not POSIX network FS.

anti_bot.quote: Sandbox SDK lets you run untrusted, AI-generated code in secure, isolated containers directly from your Cloudflare Worker.
anti_bot.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — this is a general-purpose code-execution/container sandbox, not a browser-automation product; no stealth/fingerprinting feature is documented anywhere in the Sandbox SDK or Containers docs.

captcha_solving.quote: Sandbox SDK lets you run untrusted, AI-generated code in secure, isolated containers directly from your Cloudflare Worker.
captcha_solving.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — a container/VM code-execution platform, not a browser-automation or scraping product; no CAPTCHA-solving capability is documented.

egress_ip_type.quote: Outbound handlers are programmable egress proxies that run on the same machine as the sandbox.
egress_ip_type.note: Outbound traffic leaves through Cloudflare's own network/edge (shared Cloudflare IP ranges), not a residential or mobile IP pool; no dedicated/static customer-assigned egress IP is documented (containers are placed dynamically across Cloudflare's global network, so the source IP is a shared Cloudflare datacenter IP).

live_resize.quote: The memory, vCPU, and disk space for Containers are set through instance types. ... These are specified using the instance_type property in your Worker's Wrangler configuration file.
live_resize.note: Instance type (vCPU/memory/disk) is fixed at deploy time via Wrangler config for a container class; no documented API to change CPU/RAM of an already-running instance without redeploying/recreating it.

own_agent_api.quote: Sandbox SDK lets you run untrusted, AI-generated code in secure, isolated containers directly from your Cloudflare Worker.
own_agent_api.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — Cloudflare provides the execution environment for third-party coding/browser/computer-use agents (Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Devin, Cursor) via harness_api/tutorials, but has no first-party task agent (browser/computer-use/research agent) of its own to drive.

mcp_server.quote: Install an agent of your choice, connect skills and MCP servers, and start deploying to Cloudflare — all from your editor or terminal.
mcp_server.note: Cloudflare ships general-purpose MCP servers for its API/dev-platform (DNS, Workers deploy, docs search) referenced from the Containers/Sandbox docs sidebar ('Code Mode MCP Server', 'Domain-specific MCP Servers'), but no MCP server specifically to start/stop/exec/control Sandbox or Container instances was found in the Sandbox SDK or Containers docs/llms.txt.

static_egress_ip.quote: When initially deploying a Container, Cloudflare will select various locations across our network to deploy instances to. ... If the initial container has gone to sleep, Cloudflare will once again try to find the nearest "free" instance of the Container, likely one in North America, and start an instance there.
static_egress_ip.note: Containers are placed and re-placed across Cloudflare's global network dynamically (per instance/per restart), and no product page documents a fixed/dedicated outbound IP feature for Containers or the Sandbox SDK.

hipaa.quote: HIPAA. The Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA) sets the standard for protecting sensitive patient data. Contact your account team to request the HIPAA AoC.
hipaa.note: Cloudflare offers a HIPAA Attestation of Compliance / BAA at the account/contract level (Enterprise, via account team); not verified as a Workers/Containers/Sandbox-SDK-specific listed covered service, but Cloudflare's general compliance program covers its platform.

max_session_h.quote: Cloudflare does not stop a container instance after a fixed maximum runtime. ... Cloudflare does not guarantee that any container instance will run for a set period.
max_session_h.note: No fixed maximum session/runtime is imposed; default sleepAfter=10min idle timeout is configurable/disable-able, and irregular host restarts (not a session cap) can still stop an instance.

persistent_disk.quote: Is disk persistent? What happens to my disk when my container sleeps? All disk is ephemeral. When a Container instance goes to sleep, the next time it is started, it will have a fresh disk as defined by its container image. ... You can also use FUSE to persist disk to R2 or other object storage backends.
persistent_disk.note: reviewed: proposed correction rejected (Default is ephemeral (correctly false on its own), but that's not the whole picture: first-party opt-in persistence exists. mountBucket() ('Mount S3-compatible object storage buckets as local filesystem paths', https://developers.cloudflare.com/sandbox/guides/mount-buckets/) attaches a persistent volume that survives sleep/restart (an object store, remounted each start), and createBackup()/restoreBackup() (https://developers.cloudflare.com/sandbox/concepts/backup-restore/) let a directory's contents survive across sleeps by explicit save/restore. Card already carries volumes:true and snapshot_on_demand:true, which contradicted persistent_disk:false. Correct value: true, default-off (fresh/ephemeral disk unless you opt into a bucket mount or manual backup+restore).)

pause_resume.quote: Lifecycle states Creation ... Active ... Idle After a period of inactivity (10 minutes by default, configurable via sleepAfter), the container stops to free resources. When the next request arrives, a fresh container starts. All previous state is lost and the environment resets to its initial state. ... Destruction
pause_resume.note: Only lifecycle states are Creation/Active/Idle(stop)/Destruction; Idle wipes all state and there is no Paused state where billing is reduced and state is kept ready to resume from. keepAlive just prevents Idle entirely, it isn't a pause. No pause/resume API found anywhere in the Sandbox SDK or Containers docs.

fork.quote: Lifecycle states Creation ... Active ... Idle ... Destruction
fork.note: No fork/clone API documented across the Sandbox SDK docs, Containers docs/FAQ, or the sandbox-sdk GitHub repo. Backups (createBackup/restoreBackup) can seed a fresh sandbox from a saved directory snapshot, but that is explicit save-then-restore-elsewhere, not a running-VM fork API, and it is not named 'fork' anywhere in the docs. No evidence of a clone-a-machine primitive.

fork_running.quote: Idle After a period of inactivity ... the container stops to free resources. When the next request arrives, a fresh container starts.
fork_running.note: No documented mechanism to clone a live/running sandbox without stopping it; consistent with fork=false (no fork API exists at all).

memory_snapshot_fork.quote: Container snapshots are currently in private beta
memory_snapshot_fork.note: The only whole-container (memory+disk) snapshot mechanism is a private-beta feature with no documented fork/clone-with-running-processes capability; the GA backup feature (createBackup/restoreBackup) is directory-only, no memory/processes ('Directory-level only ... no memory/processes' per card evidence). No public docs describe forking with memory/process state preserved.

nested_virt.quote: Cloudflare Containers do not support iptables manipulation. ... Use the docker:dind-rootless base image since Containers run without root privileges.
nested_virt.note: Containers run unprivileged (rootless Docker-in-Docker required, no privileged mode); no /dev/kvm, KVM, or nested-virtualization capability is documented anywhere in the Sandbox SDK or Containers docs. Consistent with the platform being one VM-isolated Linux container per instance, not a machine that exposes hardware virtualization to the guest.

desktop.quote:
## Desktop

The desktop feature was removed in `0.10.2`. The feature ran a full Linux desktop inside the sandbox for computer-use style automation. If you still need that shape, rebuild it with extensions rather than a built-in desktop API.
desktop.note: A built-in desktop feature existed but was explicitly removed; current SDK has no built-in desktop/VNC/RDP API.

browser.quote: Browser terminals ... Connect browser-based terminal UIs to sandbox shells via WebSocket.
browser.note: The only 'browser' feature documented for Sandbox SDK is browser-based terminal UIs connecting to a shell over WebSocket, not a real/managed browser running for the agent. A real headless browser ('Browser Run tools ... headless browsers powered by Browser Run for web fetches, screenshots, and CDP control') appears only in the separate Claude Managed Agents integration template, which layers Cloudflare's separate Browser Run product on top - not a feature of the Sandbox SDK/Containers product this card models.

computer_use.quote: The desktop feature was removed in `0.10.2`. The feature ran a full Linux desktop inside the sandbox for computer-use style automation.
computer_use.note: Computer-use automation depended on the removed desktop feature; no current computer-use (screenshot+click) API is documented.

public_ipv4.quote: Preview URLs are publicly accessible by default, but require a valid access token that is generated when you expose a port.
public_ipv4.note: Inbound reachability is exclusively via HTTPS preview URLs / tunnels proxied through a Worker (https://{port}-{sandbox-id}-{token}.yourdomain.com or *.trycloudflare.com); no dedicated/public IPv4 address is ever assigned to a sandbox. Card's own network.ipv4_available is already false.

gpu.quote: Each container instance runs inside its own VM, which provides strong isolation from other workloads running on Cloudflare's network. Containers should be built for the `linux/amd64` architecture, and should stay within size limits.
gpu.note: No GPU instance types are documented anywhere in Containers/Sandbox pricing, limits, or architecture pages; the product is a CPU-only linux/amd64 container platform (outside scope).

windows.quote: Containers should be built for the `linux/amd64` architecture
windows.note: Product only runs Linux (amd64) container images; no Windows machine option exists. Outside the product's scope.

macos.quote: Containers should be built for the `linux/amd64` architecture
macos.note: Product only runs Linux (amd64) container images; no macOS machine option exists. Outside the product's scope.

arm64.quote: Containers should be built for the `linux/amd64` architecture
arm64.note: Explicitly amd64-only; no arm64 instance type documented.

self_host.quote: For deploying to production, sign up for a Cloudflare account ... Deploy your Worker and container: npx wrangler deploy
self_host.note: The SDK/container bridge is open source, but running the sandboxes themselves requires deploying to Cloudflare's own Workers/Containers platform; there is no documented way to run the managed sandbox execution platform on your own infrastructure.

byoc.quote: Each running container instance is associated with ... Durable Objects ... locations across Cloudflare's network.
byoc.note: Containers/Sandbox instances always run on Cloudflare's own global network via Workers/Durable Objects placement; no option to deploy the managed service into a customer-owned cloud account (AWS/GCP/Azure) was found.

private_network.quote: For Workers bindings (KV, R2, and similar) reached by hostname from the sandbox, refer to Connect to Workers bindings.
private_network.note: Sandbox SDK's own connectivity docs list only Workers bindings (KV, R2, Durable Objects, etc.) for reaching Cloudflare resources by hostname; no VPC/private-network binding is documented there. Workers VPC (https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers-vpc/, 'Securely connect your private cloud to Cloudflare') is a separate, account-level Workers product only mentioned via the Claude Managed Agents template ('Connect agents to private internal services over Workers VPC and Mesh'), not documented as a native Sandbox SDK feature.

usage_api.quote: Billing is calculated through the Cloudflare dashboard and account invoicing. Individual sandbox usage metrics are not available through a public API; usage is reported only at account level via dashboard or monthly invoices.
usage_api.note: granularity: account-only; cost: no; Each sandbox runs as a Durable Object and is billed for vCPU-seconds, memory-seconds, disk-seconds, and Durable Object requests/duration, but no REST API or CLI endpoint allows querying per-sandbox usage. The GraphQL Analytics API and dashboard UI provide account-level aggregates only.
